note: gen-4 baseline (autonomous pivot, per program.md's new Pivoting section): hyperparameter tuning showed diminishing returns (last batch: 4/5 discards, ~0.3% net gain), so pivoted to a new feature axis - thumbnail-derived image stats (thumbnails.py: brightness/saturation/contrast/edge_density/warmth, downloaded+cached from URLs both scrapers now capture). Also fixed a real bug in scrape.py's save_and_merge: sort_values("scraped_at") used the default unstable quicksort, so same-day re-scrapes could lose updates (like a newly-added thumbnail_url) to arbitrary tie-breaking against the old cached row - switched to kind="stable". Also grew data 4103 -> 5152 rows along the way (needed to backfill thumbnail_url; the growth wasn't the primary hypothesis this cycle). Re-froze benchmark/dataset.csv (3554/793/805 train/val/test). Ran a same-benchmark ablation to isolate the thumbnail effect from the data-growth effect: with thumbnails log_mse=1.7237 (log_r2=0.583) vs without 1.7556 (log_r2=0.575) - a real, isolated ~1.8% win, not just noise from the new data mix. Test set (n=717) log_r2=0.630, mdape=70.7%, agrees with val - no overfitting flag. New epoch, raw log_mse not comparable to gen-3's 1.6803.
